details: The US Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) maintained its benchmark federal funds rate at 3.50%-3.75% during its meeting on April 29, 2026. This decision, the third consecutive hold, came with increased internal dissent among policymakers. Fed Chair Jerome Powell, in his final meeting as chair, noted that inflation remains "elevated" and highlighted "a high level of uncertainty" stemming from developments in the Middle East, which has contributed to rising global energy prices. The committee emphasized its commitment to returning inflation to its 2% objective while carefully assessing incoming data. The "higher-for-longer" stance on interest rates implies a delayed expectation for rate cuts.
title: Fed Keeps Rates Unchanged; Powell Cites Elevated Inflation, Mideast Uncertainty

details: The US annual Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index rose to 3.5% in March 2026, up from 2.8% previously, matching market expectations. Core PCE, excluding volatile food and energy prices, also rose to 3.2% year-over-year. This data, released on April 30, 2026, by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA), indicates persistent inflationary pressures. The increase is partly attributed to surging oil prices linked to ongoing geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. Such stubborn inflation reinforces the Federal Reserve's cautious monetary policy stance and reduces the likelihood of near-term interest rate cuts.
title: US PCE Inflation Hits 3.5%; Oil Prices Fuel Persistent Pressures

details: The Bank of Canada's Governing Council maintained its policy interest rate at 2.25% on April 29, 2026. The Bank noted that the Canadian economy is being affected by global events and geopolitical uncertainties, with the Middle East war significantly driving up global energy prices. This is pushing inflation higher, with CPI inflation rising from 1.8% in February to 2.4% in March. The Bank's monetary policy is focused on preventing this surge in energy prices from leading to persistent inflation while the economy adjusts to global headwinds.
title: Bank of Canada Maintains Rate, Cites Mideast War's Inflationary Impact
